Rashi on Zevachim 14b:14:1.hebrew: שמה הולכה - ופסלה בה מחשבה לרבנן, או אם עשאה זר — פסולה. [רש"י]
Rashi on Zevachim 14b:14:1.english: Is it considered conveying? - And invalid intent disqualifies it according to the Rabbis, or if a non-priest performed it, it is invalid.

Rashi on Zevachim 14b:14:2.hebrew: או לא שמה הולכה - ולא פסלה מחשבה. [רש"י]
Rashi on Zevachim 14b:14:2.english: Or is it not considered conveying? - And intent does not disqualify it.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:10:1.hebrew: מחלוקת ר' שמעון ורבנן - דמתני' היא, אי הויא עבודה אי לא. לרבי שמעון לא הויא עבודה, דהא קתני מתני': ר' שמעון מכשיר בהילוך, דלא פסל בה מחשבה בהולכה שלא ברגל, ומשום דלאו הולכה היא:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:10:1.english: The dispute of Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis - that is in the mishna: whether it is considered a service or not. According to Rabbi Shimon it is not considered a service, as the mishna teaches: Rabbi Shimon deems [the offering] valid in the case of [improper intent during] walking, as he does not disqualify [the offering] through intent during conveying not by foot, because it is not [real] conveying.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:10:2.hebrew: בהולכה רבתי כו' - מסקנא היא למילתיה דקמפרש ואומר דכי פליגי ר"ש ורבנן (בהולכה זוטרתא) [בהולכה זוטרתא פליגי] ששחט בצד המזבח וזרק, דהיינו שלא ברגל. אבל בהולכה רבתי, דהיינו ברגל, לא פליגי. ולקמן מותיב לה ממתניתין, דשמעינן מינה דבשוחט נמי רחוק מן המזבח מכשיר רבי שמעון, מדקתני "שאם רצה שוחט בצד המזבח וזורק":
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:10:2.english: With regard to greater conveying, etc. - This is the conclusion of what [the Gemara] is explaining, and it says that when Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis disagree, [they disagree with regard to lesser conveying,] where one slaughtered next to the altar and threw [the blood], which is [conveying] not by foot. But with regard to greater conveying, that is, by foot, they do not disagree. And later [the Gemara] raises an objection to this from the mishnah, from which we learn that even when one slaughters far from the altar, Rabbi Shimon deems [the offering] valid, from the fact that it teaches, "for if he wishes, he slaughters next to the altar and throws."

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:11:1.hebrew: מחכו עליה במערבא - [מחייכו עליה] דהאי שמעתא דמוקי טעמא דר"ש בהולכה זוטרתא], ולמימר דלאו הולכה היא. ואע"פ שאי אפשר לבטלה, לזו לאו עבודה היא:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:11:1.english: They laughed at it in the West - [They smiled at it], because of this teaching, which establishes the reason of Rabbi Shimon as being a minor conveyance (hola'ah), and [because it says] that it is not a conveyance. Even though it is impossible to omit it, this is not a [proper] service.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:11:2.hebrew: אלא חטאת העוף - דקיימא לן בפ' קדשי קדשים (לקמן זבחים דף סה.) דפסל בה מחשבה בהזאת דמה, שהוא עיקר עבודתה, דכתיב שם "והזה מדם החטאת על קיר" וגו', שאוחזה בגופה ומתיז דמה לקיר. והך התזה הולכה זוטרתי היא. וכיון דטעמא דר"ש משום דהולכה זוטרא לא פסל בה מחשבה, היכי פסל בהך:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:11:2.english: But a bird sin offering - For we hold, in the chapter [entitled] Kodshei Kodashim (below, Zevachim 65a), that prohibited intent disqualifies it at the sprinkling of its blood, which is the main service of that offering, as it is written there, "And he shall sprinkle of the blood of the sin offering on the wall [of the altar]" etc. — for he holds it by its body and squirts its blood against the wall. And this squirting is a minor [form of] conveying by hand. Now since the reason of Rabbi Shimon is that prohibited intent does not disqualify a minor conveying by hand, how can it disqualify in this case?

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:11:3.hebrew: אי דחשיב עליה מקמי דליפוק דם - דהיינו בהתזתה:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:11:3.english: If he intended it before the blood came out - That is, during its sprinkling:

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:11:4.hebrew: הא אמרת לא כלום היא - דהא הולכה זוטרתי היא:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:11:4.english: But you said it is nothing - For conveying [the blood] is a minor matter.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:11:5.hebrew: ואי בתר שנעקר הדם - וניתז מן הצואר, חשיב:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:11:5.english: And if [he had the intent] after the blood was uprooted - and sprayed out from the neck, he had the thought:

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:11:6.hebrew: הא איתעבידא מצוותיה - דקס"ד מכי נפק דם גמרה לה עבודת הזאתה, ואע"ג דלא מטא דם למזבח. אא"ב בהולכה רבתי פליגי, וטעמא דר"ש משום דאפשר לבטלה הוא, הא דחטאת אי אפשר לבטלה. אלא אי אמרת משום טעם דלאו הולכה היא, ובשלא ברגל פליגי, היכי פסלה בהך? הלא אין כאן מחשבה אלא בהולכה שלא ברגל. ולר' יוחנן דאמר לעיל הולכה שלא ברגל לא שמה הולכה [ולא פסיל בה מחשבה], ליכא למיפרך מהא, דכי אמר ר' יוחנן הולכה רבתי קאמר, שאין דרכה בכך. אבל השוחט בצד המזבח כו', וכן חטאת העוף שנמלקת אצל המזבח, עיקר הולכתה בכך, ומודה בה רבי יוחנן:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:11:6.english: Its mitzva has been performed - For it entered his mind [to think] that once the blood comes out, the service of sprinkling is completed, even though the blood has not reached the altar. If [the dispute between Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis] were about a "great conveyance" (walking with the blood), and Rabbi Shimon's reason is that it is possible to do it without conveying, [then] that does not apply to a sin offering, where it is impossible to do it without conveying. But if you say [that the reason is] that it is not considered a conveyance at all, and they dispute [a conveyance done] not by foot, how does [Rabbi Shimon] disqualify it with this? Surely there is no [prohibited] intent here except during a conveyance not done by foot. And according to Rabbi Yochanan, who said above that a conveyance not done by foot is not considered a conveyance [and prohibited intent does not disqualify it], one cannot raise an objection from this [case], since when Rabbi Yochanan spoke, he spoke of a "great conveyance," whose normal way is not like that. But one who slaughters at the side of the altar, etc., and likewise a bird sin offering whose nape is pinched beside the altar — the essential conveyance of these is done in just this way, and Rabbi Yochanan concedes regarding it.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:12:1.hebrew: ומאי קושיא דלמא מדפריש - דם, דפסק לה הולכה מתחלת הזאה, וישנה להזאה עד דמטי למזבח, וחיילא עלה המחשבה:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:12:1.english: And what is the difficulty? Perhaps from when it leaves - the blood: for the act of carrying ceases from the beginning of the sprinkling, and the sprinkling persists until it reaches the altar, and the [improper] thought takes effect upon it.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:13:1.hebrew: דהא בעא מיניה כו' היה מזה - בחטאת העוף, או בחטאות הפנימיות:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:13:1.english: For Rabbi Yirmeya asked him, etc. If he was sprinkling - Regarding the bird sin-offering, or the inner sin-offerings.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:13:2.hebrew: מהו - מי הויא עבודה בבעל מום ופסולה או לא, דאיכא למימר: מכי פריש דם גמרה לה:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:13:2.english: What is the halakha? - Is it considered a service performed by a blemished priest, and is it therefore invalid, or not? For one could say: from the time the blood separated [from the bird], it had completed it.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:13:3.hebrew: וא"ל פסולה מ"ט והזה - הכוונה דחטאת העוף או דחטאות הפנימיות, דכתיב בהן הזאה. "והזה ונתן" בעינן, הזאה דומיא דנתן, דגבי הדדי כתיבי: "והזה מן הדם" וגו', "ונתן הכהן מן הדם על קרנות" וגו'. אלמא ישנה להזאה עד שיגיע למזבח:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:13:3.english: And he said to him: It is invalid. What is the reason? "And he shall sprinkle" - This refers to the sin-offering of a bird, or to the inner sin-offerings, regarding which sprinkling is written. We require "and he shall sprinkle … and he shall place," [that is,] sprinkling similar to placing, since they are written next to each other: "And he shall sprinkle of the blood" etc., "And the priest shall place of the blood upon the horns" etc. Evidently, the sprinkling is still in progress (it still exists) until [the blood] reaches the altar:

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:14:1.hebrew: היינו חוכא - הא דמחכו במערבא, משום דקשיא להו הכי:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:14:1.english: This is the laughter - That which they laughed in the West (Eretz Yisrael), [they did so] because this [matter] was difficult for them.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:14:2.hebrew: ובהולכה רבתי לא פליגי והא כי פליגי כו' - דהא דקתני אפשר שלא בהילוך, ש"מ בדהילוך עסקינן, וטעם משום שאפשר לבטלה הוא, והא מיהא לא ביטל:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:14:2.english: And with regard to greater conveying they do not disagree? But when they disagree, etc. - For [from the fact] that [the mishnah] teaches "it is possible without conveying," we learn that we are dealing with [a case of] conveying by foot; and the reason is that it is possible to dispense with it, and this one, at least, he did not dispense with.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:15:1.hebrew: אלא בהולכה זוטרתי כ"ע לא פליגי דפסולה גרסינן - וטעמא, משום דא"א לבטל. ומאן דגריס "דלא פסלה", טעמא משום דלאו כלום היא, ואין שם הולכה עליה, אלא כולה צורך זריקה היא, והא לא הוה בדעתיה למחשב אזריקה אלא אהולכה, ולא חשיב מידי. ופסול דחטאת העוף, כדאוקי מדפריש ועד דמטא למזבח, ומשום מחשבת הזאה ולא משום מחשבת הולכה:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:15:1.english: Rather, with regard to lesser conveying, everyone agrees that it disqualifies; this is the text we read - And the reason is because it is impossible to nullify [the intent]. But as for the one who reads "that it does not disqualify," the reason is that it is nothing, and the name "conveying" does not apply to it; rather, all of it is a need of the throwing [of the blood]. And [the person] did not intend to think about the throwing but only about the conveying, and so it counts for nothing. And the disqualification of the bird sin-offering, as [the Gemara] established it as applying from when he separates [the bird's head] until he reaches the altar, is on account of improper intent regarding the sprinkling and not on account of improper intent regarding the conveying.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:16:1.hebrew: הוליכו זר - ברגל. והחזירו כהן, שהעבודה עליו מוטלת, וחזר והוליכו — כשר. והא דתניא לעיל זר ואונן בהולכה פסול — כשלא הוחזרה:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:16:1.english: A non-priest conveyed it - On foot (i.e., by walking it to the altar). And a priest returned it, since the service is incumbent upon him, and he again conveyed it — it is valid. And that which was taught above, that a non-priest and an onen [a priest in the first day of mourning] who perform conveying [of the blood] are unfit — [that refers to a case] where it was not returned.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:16:2.hebrew: אפשר לתקונה - אפשר לתקן להולכת פסול, ולא דמיא לשאר עבודות. דאילו שחיטה וקבלה וזריקה, מאחר שנעשו בפסול, אי אפשר לחזור ולעשותן בהכשר. וא"ת קבלה נמי יש לתקן, כגון שלא קבל הפסול כל הדם, ויכול כשר לחזור ולקבל — ההיא ודאי כשרה, ובפ' שלישי (לקמן זבחים דף לב.) תנן לה: אם יש דם הנפש יחזור הכשר ויקבל, וכן בזריקה:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:16:2.english: It is possible to correct it - It is possible to correct a conveyance [of the blood] that was performed improperly, and it is not similar to the other service acts. For with slaughter, receiving, and sprinkling, once they have been performed improperly, it is impossible to go back and perform them properly. And if you say that receiving too can be corrected — for example, where the disqualified person did not receive all the blood, and a fit person can go back and receive [the rest] — that [case] is certainly valid; and in the third chapter (below, Zevachim 32a) we learned it: if there is [still] blood of the life-force, the fit person should go back and receive, and the same applies to sprinkling.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:17:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן - הוליכו כהן והחזירו, וחזר והוליכו זר:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:17:1.english: This is how we read: "A priest conveyed it, and returned it, and a non-priest again conveyed it":

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:17:2.english: Rav Shimi said: According to the one who deems [it] fit - in the case where a non-priest conveyed it, and a priest returned it and conveyed it again:

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:17:3.hebrew: פוסל - כיון דהתם, מ"ט מכשיר? דאזיל בתר בתרייתא, ה"נ זיל בתר בתרייתא:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:17:3.english: Deems unfit - Since there, what is the reason [that he] deems [it] fit? [It is] because he follows the last [conveyance]; here too, follow the last.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:17:4.hebrew: לדברי הפוסל - דאזיל בתר הולכה קמייתא, מכשיר, כיון דאזיל בתר קמייתא:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:17:4.english: According to the statement of the one who deems [it] unfit - For he follows the first conveyance; here he deems [it] fit, since he follows the first [conveyance].

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:17:5.hebrew: אף לדברי הפוסל פוסל כאן, דהא צריך לאמטוייה [מאחר שנתרחק צריך לחזור ולהביאו לצד מזבח, נמצא דהולכה אחרונה לצורך ככל ההולכות]:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:17:5.english: Even according to the one who deems [the offering] unfit [in the previous case], he deems it unfit here, for it needs to be brought [back]. [Since it was distanced, it must return and be brought to the side of the altar. It turns out that the final conveyance is necessary, like all the conveyances.]

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:1:1.hebrew: אפשר לתקנה - בין שעשאה זר בין שעשאה כהן, אמרינן דאין הולכה ופסולה, דהא נעשית שלא כהלכתה. מיהו, יש לה תקנה להחזירה לאחוריה ולחזור להוליך ברגל, או אין לה תקנה:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:1:1.english: Is it possible to correct it - Whether a non-priest performed it or a priest performed it, we say that [conveying the blood by hand] is not [valid] conveying and is disqualified, since it was done not in its proper manner. However, [the question is whether] there is a way to correct it, by returning [the blood] backward and conveying it again by foot, or whether there is no way to correct it.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:2:1.english: He should return it to the fit [priest] - Evidently, it is possible to correct it.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:3:1.hebrew: ונהי נמי כו' - כלומר, ואי נמי מפרשת לה דבכשר ראשון [שיוליך] לצד המזבח קאמר, וכל שכן דשמעת דהולכת כשר קמא דהואי שלא ברגל כשרה היא, מכל מקום ש"מ דכשרה ע"י תקנה:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:3:1.english: And though indeed, etc. - That is to say: Even if you explain it as referring to the first, fit [priest] who [will carry the blood] to the side of the altar, then all the more so you have heard that the conveying by the first fit priest, which was not done by foot, is valid. In any case, we learn that it is valid through correction.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:3:2.english: It was disqualified - through the first conveyance by the fit [priest].

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:4:1.hebrew: מי סברת דקאי זר גואי - דקאי לצד המזבח, ואז נמצא שהקריב הראשון בהושטתו לצד המזבח:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:4:1.english: Do you maintain that the non-priest is standing inside - on the side of the altar, [so that] the first [priest] brought [the blood] closer by extending it toward the altar?

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:4:2.hebrew: דקאי זר בראי - וכשר שהושיטה לו, הרחיקה מן המזבח. הלכך לאו הולכה הואי לפסול. וכי פשטינן, יחזור כשר ויטלנו, וזר מעשה איצטבא הוא דעבד, דליכא הושטת יד המקרבתו למזבח:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:4:2.english: That the non-priest is standing outside - And the fit [priest] who extended [the blood] to him distanced it from the altar. Therefore, it was not conveying for the disqualified [person]. And when we say that the fit [priest] should return and take it [from him], [this is because] the non-priest merely performed an act of [placing it on a] bench, for there was no extension of the hand that brings it closer to the altar:

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:5:1.hebrew: פסלה - ואפילו עשאה כהן, פוסלת הדם. וההיא דפסחים, בדניידי, וכדשנינן:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:5:1.english: It disqualifies it - Even if a Kohen performed it, it disqualifies the blood. And that [ruling] in Pesachim is [speaking of a case] where they moved [the blood along], as we answered.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:6:1.hebrew: נשפך מן הכלי על הרצפה ואספו כשר - הואיל ונתקבל בכלי. משנה היא בפ' שלישי של מסכת זבחים (בכל הפסולים). קס"ד: כשנשפך ונתפשט ברצפה, נתקרב לצד המזבח, וקתני כשר. ונהי נמי דאמרת דצריך להחזירו לאחוריו ולחזור ולהוליך ברגל, מ"מ בתקנתא סגי לה:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:6:1.english: If it spilled from the vessel onto the floor and one collected it, it is fit - Since it was already received in a vessel. This is a mishna in the third chapter (Kol HaPesulin). The Gemara thought: when it spilled and spread on the floor, it was brought closer to the side of the altar, and yet the mishna teaches that it is fit. And even though you say that one must return it backward and then go again by foot, nevertheless it is enough for it to be corrected.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:7:1.hebrew: כשיצא לחוץ - כשנשפך, לא נתפשט לצד המזבח, אלא נתפשט להלן מן המזבח ונתרחק:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:7:1.english: When it went outward - When it was spilled, it did not spread toward the altar, but spread away from the altar and became distant.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:8:1.hebrew: ופרכינן לבראי נפיק לגואי לא עייל - בתמיה, וכי אפשר לדם צלול שישפך ולא יתפשט לכל צדדין:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:8:1.english: And we ask: It goes out [but] does not come in - [This is] an incredulous question: Is it possible for fluid blood to be spilled and not spread to all sides?

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:8:2.english: On an inclined place - And it slopes outside the altar.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:8:3.english: In a hole - For [the blood] stays in its place and does not spread out.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:8:4.hebrew: אי נמי בסמיכא - דם עבה וקרוב לקרוש:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:8:4.english: Alternatively, where it is thick - Blood that is thick and close to congealed.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:9:1.english: In the other chapter - In the second chapter.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:9:2.hebrew: נשפך על הרצפה - מצואר בהמה, ולא נתקבל בכלי:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:9:2.english: Spilled onto the floor - From the animal's neck, and it was not received in a vessel.

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:9:3.hebrew: לפלוג בדידיה - בההיא דפרק שלישי דאיירי בקבלת כלי, נפלוג בה חילוק לפסול, שפעמים שאף מן הכלי לרצפה פסול. אלא מדלא אשכח פסול אלא מצואר בהמה, ש"מ נשפך מן הכלי, לא שנא נפק לבראי ול"ש עייל לגואי, כשר:
Rashi on Zevachim 15a:9:3.english: Let it distinguish within the case itself - In that [mishnah] of the third chapter, which deals with receiving [the blood] in a vessel, let it make a distinction in it to render [the blood] unfit, since sometimes even [blood that went] from the vessel to the floor is unfit. But since it found [a case of] unfitness only [where the blood spilled] from the animal's neck, we conclude [that when the blood] spilled from the vessel, it makes no difference whether it went outward or whether it came inward — [it is] fit:

Rashi on Zevachim 15a:9:4.english: A refutation - This is a refutation of Ulla.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Zevachim 14b:14.english: The main question is whether the mitzva of conveying was fulfilled by this, and if one did not convey it by foot, he did not fulfill it (see Rashi at the end of this page, and also the student of Rav Pappa in Shita Mekubbetzet, Keren Ora). However, Rashi adds that there are two additional implications to this: if it is considered conveying, then if one had an invalid intent at that time, it disqualifies the offering, and similarly, conveying not by foot by a non-priest is invalid. But if it is not considered conveying, then the intent does not disqualify it, and similarly, if a non-priest conveyed it not by foot, it is not considered to disqualify the offering.

Steinsaltz on Zevachim 14b:14.english: A dilemma was raised before them [it was asked to the scholars]: Is conveying not by foot, meaning one did not walk to the altar but rather, for example, transferred the blood basin by hand, considered conveying or not considered conveying?

Tosafot on Zevachim 14b:14:1.hebrew: (כל זה בהג"ה דאיבעיא להו) איבעיא להו הולכה שלא ברגל שמה הולכה או לא - פירש רש"י: לפסול בה מחשבה וגם בזר. דאי שמה הולכה, מחשבה שלא לשמו או פיגול פוסלת בה. ואי לא שמה הולכה, אינה קרויה עבודה, וצריך להחזיר המזרק אחריו ולעשות הולכה ברגל. וגם אם עשאה זר או יושב אין בכך כלום ויכול לתקנה בכהן בהולכת רגל. [אבל] דכהן, או אם זר מוליך בהולכת רגל, פסולה ואינו יכול לתקנה בכהן להחזירה ולהוליכה כהן. וקאמר ת"ש: וכן יושב פסול. הא עומד דומיא דיושב שאינו זז ממקומו כשר. אלמא הויא הולכה ועשה עבודה כתקנה. ולכך נמי כי עשאה מיושב פסול, דכתיב לעמוד לשרת. אבל מיושב פסול לא מצי מוכח דהויא הולכה עבודה בלאו דיוקא, משום דדלמא לאו עבודה היא ויושב פסול היינו כי לא תקנה ולא החזיר הדם לאחוריו לעשות הולכה אחרת. [תוספות]
Tosafot on Zevachim 14b:14:1.english: (All this is in the gloss of 'A dilemma was raised to them') A dilemma was raised to them: Is conveying not by foot considered conveying or not? - Rashi explains that this is regarding whether intent or a non-priest can disqualify it. For if it *is* considered conveying, then intent not for its sake or *piggul* (improper intent regarding time) disqualifies it. But if it is *not* considered conveying, it is not called a sacrificial rite, and one must return the basin and perform conveying by foot. Furthermore, if a non-priest or a sitting priest performed it, there is no consequence, and it can be rectified by a priest conveying by foot. However, if a priest (properly) conveys by foot, or if a non-priest conveys by foot (invalidly), it is invalid and cannot be rectified by a priest returning it and conveying it (again). And the Gemara says 'Come and hear' (a proof): 'And likewise, a sitting priest is invalid.' But a standing priest, similar to a sitting priest who does not move from his place, is valid. Apparently, it *is* considered conveying, and he performed the rite properly. Therefore, when he performed it while sitting, it is invalid, as it is written 'to stand to serve.' However, from 'a sitting priest is invalid,' one cannot prove that it is conveying as a rite without this inference, because perhaps it is not a rite, and 'a sitting priest is invalid' means that he did not rectify it and did not return the blood backwards to perform another conveying.

Tosafot on Zevachim 15a:10:1.hebrew: הולכה שלא ברגל מחלוקת ר"ש ורבנן - יש מפרש פירוש אחר, אבל פירוש הקונטרס עיקר:
Tosafot on Zevachim 15a:10:1.english: "Conveying not by foot is the dispute of Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis" - There is one who explains [this] with a different explanation, but the explanation of the Kuntres [i.e., Rashi] is the primary one:

Tosafot on Zevachim 15a:11:1.hebrew: חטאת העוף דפסלה [הזאה] היכי משכחת לה - כיון דמכשיר ר"ש בהולכה שלא ברגל, אלא ודאי אפכא מסתברא, ותלוי הדבר באפשר לבטלה: דרחוק מן המזבח, הולכה זו [אפשר לבטלה], דאי בעי הוה שחיט בצד המזבח ולא פסלה בה מחשב'; אבל שחט קרוב למזבח, דהולכה זו של הושטת יד לא אפשר לבטלה — פסלה בה מחשבה. ולהכי בחטאת העוף פסלה מחשבה בהזאה מכי נפיק עד דמטא למזבח, דלא אפשר לבטל דבר זה. אבל לאידך, דלא תליא באפשר ולא אפשר, אלא הולכה שלא ברגל לא חשיבא והוי כאילו איתעביד — אם כן בחטאת העוף נמי כאילו אתעביד מצותו. ומשני: דרחמנא מחשבה זו מחשבה שלימה ברו"ך:
Tosafot on Zevachim 15a:11:1.english: A bird sin offering, where [sprinkling] is disqualified — how can one find [such a case]? - Since Rabbi Shimon validates [an offering when the intent was during] conveying not done on foot, rather, certainly the opposite is more reasonable, and the matter depends on whether it is possible to avoid it: When [the animal is slaughtered] far from the altar, this conveying [is something it is] possible to avoid, for if one wished, one could have slaughtered beside the altar, and intent during it would not disqualify it. But if one slaughtered close to the altar, where this conveying is [merely] the extending of the hand, which it is not possible to avoid — intent during it disqualifies. And therefore, in the case of a bird sin offering, intent disqualifies it during the sprinkling, from when [the blood] comes out until it reaches the altar, because it is not possible to avoid this act. But according to the other [explanation], which does not depend on whether it is possible or not possible [to avoid it], but rather that conveying not done on foot is not regarded [as significant] and it is as if it were already performed — then in the case of a bird sin offering too, it is as if its mitzvah had been performed. And [the Gemara] answers: that the Merciful One [treats] this intent as complete intent. Blessed be the Lord.

Tosafot on Zevachim 15a:11:2.hebrew: אלא חטאת העוף דפסלה בה מחשבה היכי משכחת לה - אי אמרת בשלמא בהולכה (שלא ברגל) פליגי, אבל בזוטרתי דלא אפשר לבטלה פסלה מחשבה, משכחת לה מיקמי דתיפוק דם, משום דדם הנתון בצואר כנתון בכלי שרת. ולא דמי לבעיא דרבי אבין בריש דם חטאת (לקמן זבחים דף צב:), דאיבעיא ליה אי צואר ככלי שרת אי לא. אבל אי בזוטרתי לא פסלה לר' שמעון, היכי משכחת לה? אבל מכל זריקה דעלמא לא קשיא ליה: אי מיקמי דליפוק דם מן הכלי לאו כלום הוא, ואי בתר דנפק הא איתעביד ליה מצותו, משום [דמדמפריש] ליה עד דמטא לא איתעביד מצותו. אבל בהזאה סד"א דלא צריך מזבח, מידי דהוה אהזאה דפרוכת ובין הבדים דהויא הזאה אע"פ שלא נגע. הגה"ה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 15a:11:2.english: But a bird sin offering, which is disqualified by [improper] intent — how can one find [such a case]? - If you say, granted, that they disagree about conveying [the blood] (not on foot), but regarding the small [amount of blood], which cannot be nullified, [improper] intent disqualifies it, one can find such a case before the blood comes out, since blood placed on the neck is like [blood] placed in a sacred vessel. And this is not like the question of Rabbi Avin in the beginning of [the chapter] Dam Chatat (below, Zevachim 92b), where he asked whether the neck is like a sacred vessel or not. But if with the small [amount of blood] intent does not disqualify according to Rabbi Shimon, how can one find [such a case]? But with any other throwing in general, this is not difficult for him: if [the intent was] before the blood left the vessel, it is nothing, and if after it left, its mitzvah was already performed, because [from the time] he separates it until it arrives [at the altar], its mitzvah has not yet been performed. But with sprinkling, I might have thought that the altar is not needed, just as with the sprinkling toward the curtain and between the staves, which is [valid] sprinkling even though it did not touch. Gloss.

Zevachim 14b:14.english: A dilemma was raised before the scholars: Is conveying the blood not by foot, but rather by passing it by hand to another priest, considered conveying, or is it not considered conveying? Can the rite be performed in this manner?

Zevachim 15a:10.english: It was stated: Is conveying the blood not by foot considered conveying or not? This is a dispute between Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis in our mishna, as to whether prohibited intent disqualifies such conveying. The explanation is as follows: With regard to major conveying, which is conveying the blood by moving one's feet to the altar, everyone agrees that it disqualifies the offering. When they disagree, it is with regard to minor conveying, where one slaughtered the offering right next to the altar. Rabbi Shimon holds that it is not conveying, and therefore prohibited intent does not disqualify it, while the Rabbis deem it unfit.

Zevachim 15a:16.english: If a non-priest conveyed the blood to the altar, and a priest returned it to its original location, and a priest then conveyed it again to the altar, the sons of Rabbi Ḥiyya and Rabbi Yannai disagree with regard to the halakha. One of them says that the offering is fit, and the other says it is unfit. This is because one Sage holds that if the blood is conveyed improperly, it is possible to correct it, and the other Sage holds that it is not possible to correct it if it was initially performed improperly.
